definition: A free-text summary describing the event, situation, or record.
The kind of numeric or categorical value a metric carries (count, proportion, ratio, currency amount, index, duration, nominal, ordinal, qualitative).

The unit of measure for a metric. May be a UCUM unit code, an ISO 4217 currency code for currency amounts, the SDMX UNIT_MEASURE code 'PT' for percentages, or the literal 'unitless' for proportions expressed in 0..1.
SDMX-style scale exponent. 0 for units, 3 for thousands, 6 for millions, 9 for billions. Default 0.
The number of decimal places to use when reporting the metric.
The ordered list of MetricDimension references that disaggregate this metric. Ordering drives the DSD round-trip and the column order on SDMX-CSV emission.
The list of MetricAttribute references that may decorate observations, series, or the dataset for this metric.
The single primary computation that turns PublicSchema record-level data into a value for this metric. Variant computations are carried by libraries.

The substantive topic family of the metric (coverage, adequacy, expenditure, leakage, targeting, inclusion error, exclusion error, regularity, processing time, satisfaction). Drives browsing and faceting on the website.
The skos:Concept URI this metric, dimension, or attribute realises. Multiple metrics may share a single concept_uri when they measure the same underlying notion through different operationalisations.

Optional URI tagging this metric with a metric-family group. Metrics sharing a family value also share dimensions and observation-level attributes; the family value drives DSD generation. Modelled as a tag rather than a separate MetricFamily class until there are at least three real families. Named metric_family to avoid collision with the family slot in schema/civil_status.yaml.

External URIs to which this metric, dimension, or attribute aligns: SDMX agency DSDs, UN SDG indicators, ASPIRE families, ESSPROS reference metadata, SOCX DSDs, DHIS2 indicator UIDs, IATI indicator codes, HXL hashtags. Alignment is one-way semantic; PublicSchema does not synchronise with these registries.

True if the metric belongs to the core tier (shipped with every PublicSchema deployment), false if it belongs to the extended tier (opt-in, country or program-specific). Per design-principles.md principle 9.
The version identifier of an artefact such as an instrument, software agent, scoring rule, or privacy notice (for example, a release date such as 2022-10-11 or a semantic version like 6.2).
URI of the metric record that this metric supersedes.
URI of the metric record that supersedes this metric.
